name: shipyard-tools
title: Coding sessions: other tools on the same questions

conditions.corpus: the shipyard corpus: 32 sessions, 30 held-out questions, each asked in the session's own terms and paraphrased
conditions.tools: each at its defaults and a recorded version, in a container with only the corpus mounted and the network off while searching; commands in bench/shipyard/results/README.md
conditions.scoring: every session holding the answer among the first five distinct sessions returned; no model involved
conditions.versions: cass v0.11.0; episodic-memory 1.6.0 (7e06519); agentmemory v0.9.33; TraceDecay v0.0.74
conditions.not run: claude-mem 15.18.1 cannot load existing transcripts without a model provider, so it is not runnable under this protocol

summary: The same held-out questions, given to four other tools that search past agent sessions. Three of them can use embeddings as well as keywords; ctx uses keywords only.
baseline: ctx on the same questions (28 of 30 in the session's own terms, 5 of 30 paraphrased), with a sign test on the paired questions
bar: a difference counts only if a sign test on the paired held-out questions gives p below 0.05 (set in bench/head-to-head.md before the run)
meaning: In the session's own terms every tool that ran properly is level with ctx; only TraceDecay was worse (p = 0.008). Paraphrased, the three tools using embeddings are clearly better than ctx: cass found 23 of 30, episodic-memory 20 and agentmemory 17, against ctx's 5 (each p below 0.001). That is the real gap in ctx's search. It costs them indexing time: one to nineteen minutes for 32 sessions, against seconds for keyword indexes. cass with keywords alone scored 1 of 30 because its default search needs every word of the question to match; that is its default, not its ceiling. This measures finding the session only. In the separate answer test, paraphrasing barely changed what agents got right, because agents rewrite their searches.
